newsitem.title: DENMARK: Lauritzen says expects progress in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Lauritzen says expects progress in 1997.

text.p: Danish shipping and shipbuilding group J.Lauritzen said on Monday it upheld previous expectations of making "a certain amount of progress" in 1997.
"Our expectations for 1997 are unchanged, we expect to see a certain advance compared to 1996," Lauritzen managing director Claus Ipsen told Reuters.

On Friday Lauritzen's Lauritzen Reefers unit sold two refrigeration ships to Finland's Helsinki-based Hollming Shipping and bought another two ships from it, saying that the transaction would bring in considerable financial gains.

Lauritzen, hit by problems with its Danyard shipbuilding operations including stiff competition, adverse currency movements and productivity, posted a 259 million crown net loss for full year 1996, compared to the previous year's 832 million crown shortfall.

In June, Lauritzen said that payment for the sale of a 48 percent stake in Danyard to Malaysia's Penang Shipbuilding Construction (PSC) could be delayed beyond its August target, as approval was still awaited from the Malaysian government.
Ipsen said that while it expected to do better this year with the stronger dollar helping earnings, Lauritzen would not post an acceptable result until 1998.
"We won't be satisfied until then, " he said.
